regions.name: Hearthmere
regions.subtitle: THE BELL THAT FORGOT MORNING
regions.arrival: The morning bell has not rung in thirteen days. At first the village enjoyed the quiet. Then the bread forgot how to rise. Yesterday, a child forgot the word for home.|Nara gives you an empty field book. A keeper does not own a spirit, she says. A keeper remembers what a spirit chooses to be. Three small travellers wait beside the road. One will walk with you.
regions.epilogue: The Hearth Bell rings without asking another bell to answer for it. The baker's dough rises. The child points at the inn and says home.|Nara remembers the fire. This time, she also remembers the people who helped rebuild. Sable takes the eastern road before dawn, leaving a repaired bridge behind.

sites.name: Hearth Inn
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: A warm light marks a place where nobody has to earn their rest. All your companions recover here. Three field remedies are replenished freely.|You can arrange your party, choose a lead, and tune a companion's temperament in the spirit book. Bond ranks unlock additional starting charms. No companion is lost when a challenge goes badly.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

sites.name: Nara's Field Book
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: I once kept the road between eight sanctuaries. Their bells carried names through the valley. When one bell fell silent, I tied its note to another. Then another. I thought I was helping.|Now every sound leads toward the Crown. Find the spirits by the old footbridge. Meet their challenge, and listen after the dust settles. That is how trust begins.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Ember Footbridge
sites.speaker: Cinderfox / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: It has arranged fallen twigs into a tiny hearth. Whenever the flame gutters, it offers another bright tail-spark. Nara says it follows travellers who know when to stop running.|FIELD NOTE / Move through its first flame, then give yourself room to recover. Its short reach makes chasing and retreating very different decisions.
sites.after: The fox leaves one coal beside your boot. It stays warm even after the rain.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The First Breathing Space
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: A keeper has prepared a two-spirit relay. Your party shares its condition across the rounds. Observe a telegraph, make a deliberate move, and leave energy for the answer.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: The Baker's Bowl
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: The baker has been leaving bowls of milk for a creature made of embers. It cannot drink them. It comes anyway, to keep the bowls warm.|A name is not a description. It is a promise to notice someone again. Write that down before you go.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Bramble Clearing
sites.speaker: Brambleback / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: A walking shrine blocks the path. Paper wishes flutter among its thorns. It will not move until somebody reads the smallest wish, written by a child who simply wanted a friend.|FIELD NOTE / Its rooted defense is strongest when you hurry into it. Draw out a commitment, then approach from another angle.
sites.after: A fresh paper wish appears beneath the shrine roof. There is no name on it yet.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: A Place to Stand
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: The second relay asks you to read the whole garden: obstacles, the central sanctuary, and the direction of the wind. Winning by holding ground is as valid as a knockout.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Paper Lantern Path
sites.speaker: Quillrat / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Quillrat has collected every discarded shopping list in the village. It sorts them by the things people forgot. At the top of the pile is a note that says only: come home early.|FIELD NOTE / A prickly defender invites wasteful attacks. Wait for its resources to fall, then use an opening rather than a constant barrage.
sites.after: A folded scrap appears in your field book. It is a list of places the two of you have not visited.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Crooked Sapling
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: The gardener has been pruning the orchard into perfect circles. The Orchardboar keep planting crooked saplings in the gaps.|Let one corner grow however it likes, you suggest. The gardener considers this a much more frightening experiment than any duel.|REQUEST / Bring three different spirit friends to the sapling. A crooked garden needs more than one kind of root.
sites.after: Some problems become smaller when someone takes time to ask the right question.|Your companions gain 60 bond experience. You receive 12 memory threads and a keepsake recorded in the journal.

sites.name: Between Thorn and Flame
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: The third relay changes the opposing species. A strategy that chased the first spirit may exhaust itself against the next. Choose your lead before entering.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Dewpool
sites.speaker: Dewotter / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Dewotter has tied a ribbon around every raindrop it could catch. By noon the ribbons are empty. It keeps them anyway, because the rain was here.|FIELD NOTE / Cleansing and return paths can reverse an exchange. Commit after the protective answer, and watch where the water will travel back.
sites.after: An empty blue ribbon joins your book. It smells faintly of the river.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: Sable at the Bridge
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: Sable is repairing the bridge alone. They wear the badge of the Census, the order that numbered every spirit in the valley.|If we could make them predictable, nobody would lose a home to a wandering storm, they say. You cannot dismiss that wish. But a number is a poor substitute for a conversation.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: A Promise Kept
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: The last road trial asks you to bring everything together. Stop when an art requires planting. A short dodge creates an opening; endless sideways travel spends your recovery.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Orchard Hollow
sites.speaker: Orchardboar / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Orchardboar plants crooked saplings where the gardener wanted a straight fence. Every sapling has survived the storms. The fence has been replaced three times.|FIELD NOTE / A broad body can control a narrow lane. Use committed forward pressure thoughtfully; reversing out of every exchange gives away too much ground.
sites.after: The gardener leaves a gap in the new fence.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Travel Chest
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: A traveller has left supplies for whoever follows: five memory threads and two field remedies. Nothing here has a price tag. Take what you need, and remember the gesture.
sites.after: The chest is empty. Someone on another road may need the same kindness.

sites.name: Three Morning Bells
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: The leaf wakes first. The ember warms its roots. The tide puts the ember to sleep.
sites.after: The bells have found their own voices. Eight memory threads are yours to carry.

sites.name: The Hearth Bell
sites.speaker: The Hearth Bell
sites.text: The Hearth Bell contains one of Nara's memories: a village burning, a young keeper promising that nothing would ever surprise her again.|The bell challenges your companions. Do not rush every opening. Let them breathe. A road cannot begin with an exhausted traveller.
sites.after: The Hearth Bell rings without asking another bell to answer for it. The baker's dough rises. The child points at the inn and says home.|Nara remembers the fire. This time, she also remembers the people who helped rebuild. Sable takes the eastern road before dawn, leaving a repaired bridge behind.

sites.name: The Eastern Road
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: The restored bell has opened the next road. You may travel onward or use the atlas to revisit any sanctuary you have reached.
sites.after: The road remains open. The spirits here will remember you.

sites.name: Hearth Relay
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: A five-spirit endurance relay for a well-rested party. Conditions carry across rounds. There is no entry fee, and no penalty beyond returning to the sanctuary.|This optional trial rewards mastery and memory threads. The main road never requires repeating it.
sites.after: The relay is complete. You can return with another party whenever you wish.

sites.name: The First Field Book
sites.speaker: Keeper Nara
sites.text: A page from Nara's first field book: If a spirit leaves, leave a place for it. If it returns, do not ask where it has been before offering tea.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

regions.request: Bring three different spirit friends to the sapling. A crooked garden needs more than one kind of root.

regions.name: Reedglass Fen
regions.subtitle: A RIVER WITH TWO MEMORIES
regions.arrival: Reedglass has two maps. One shows the river where it flows. The other shows where it flowed before the flood. The villagers argue over which is correct.|At dusk, the old river appears in the air above the new one. Boats drift through kitchen windows. The ferryman charges the same fare on both.
regions.epilogue: The old river stops passing through walls. It remains as a pale line on the water, visible at sunset.|Ivo hangs both maps beside the landing. One tells you how to travel. The other tells you why the village keeps a light on for strangers.

sites.name: The Ferry House
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: A warm light marks a place where nobody has to earn their rest. All your companions recover here. Three field remedies are replenished freely.|You can arrange your party, choose a lead, and tune a companion's temperament in the spirit book. Bond ranks unlock additional starting charms. No companion is lost when a challenge goes badly.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

sites.name: Two Maps
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: I carried a woman across this river for forty years. When the flood took her house, the Census moved her name to a safer bank. Now she remembers two homes and cannot find either.|The spirits are caught between currents. Water carries more than a body. Watch its direction before you plant your feet.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Mudskipper Bank
sites.speaker: Miretoad / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: A tiny ferry made of leaves circles Miretoad. Its passengers are pebbles from opposite banks. The spirit is convinced that every stone deserves a chance to see the other shore.|FIELD NOTE / Mud and lingering danger punish a predictable route. Cross decisively, then find dry ground for your next cast.
sites.after: It appoints your smallest button captain of the leaf ferry.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: Crossing the Current
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: A keeper has prepared a two-spirit relay. Your party shares its condition across the rounds. Observe a telegraph, make a deliberate move, and leave energy for the answer.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Glass Reed
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: A glass reed repeats the last sentence spoken beside it. Thousands of reeds are whispering: We will come back for you.|Nobody remembers who said it first. You leave a marker for the lost crossing instead of pulling the reeds out.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: The Upper Mill
sites.speaker: Tidecoil / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Tidecoil has tied a loose knot around a drifting bottle. Inside is a letter addressed to the river. The spirit insists on delivering it upstream, where the river was younger.|FIELD NOTE / Currents carry both bodies and projectiles. Look at the whole vector field before deciding which side of the garden is safe.
sites.after: The bottle disappears around a bend. The current returns with a clear blue ribbon.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: Two Banks, One River
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: The second relay asks you to read the whole garden: obstacles, the central sanctuary, and the direction of the wind. Winning by holding ground is as valid as a knockout.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Widow's Weir
sites.speaker: Kelpwidow / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Kelpwidow is weaving a net with a door in it. The fisher says this defeats the purpose. The spirit says a good net should catch stories, not decide how long they stay.|FIELD NOTE / A prepared web punishes entering on its terms. Draw out a control move and approach through the space it did not cover.
sites.after: The first story to pass through is yours.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Borrowed Thread
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: The net maker believes a Kelpwidow has stolen her best thread. The spirit has woven it into a cradle for river eggs.|The net maker asks for a drawing, then makes a second cradle. The first lesson in collection is knowing when to leave something where it belongs.|REQUEST / Befriend a spirit from the Fen and read the memory at the old river marker. The ferryman needs a witness from each bank.
sites.after: Some problems become smaller when someone takes time to ask the right question.|Your companions gain 60 bond experience. You receive 12 memory threads and a keepsake recorded in the journal.

sites.name: The Narrow Crossing
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: The third relay changes the opposing species. A strategy that chased the first spirit may exhaust itself against the next. Choose your lead before entering.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Salt Landing
sites.speaker: Saltcrab / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Saltcrab sorts the beach into grains that came from mountains and grains that came from shells. The piles collapse whenever the tide returns. It calls this excellent research.|FIELD NOTE / A guarded front is an invitation to consider another approach. Energy and turning speed decide whether that approach is actually affordable.
sites.after: It gives you a grain from each pile and asks for no promise to keep them apart.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Gate Order
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: Sable has built a gate that makes the river flow in one direction. It saves the lower houses and strands every Tidecoil above the mill.|A system can be useful and still need to change. Sable agrees to open the gate for one hour. Help the spirits find the passage before the water settles.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: The Open Sluice
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: The last road trial asks you to bring everything together. Stop when an art requires planting. A short dodge creates an opening; endless sideways travel spends your recovery.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Spindle Marsh
sites.speaker: Latchspider / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Latchspider has fastened the two halves of a broken ferry ticket together. It thinks this should bring the ferry back. The ferryman sits beside it until the next tide.|FIELD NOTE / Anchors and traps turn familiar ground into a commitment. Reassess a safe spot after each new setup.
sites.after: The mended ticket becomes a bookmark.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: Ferryman's Cache
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: A traveller has left supplies for whoever follows: five memory threads and two field remedies. Nothing here has a price tag. Take what you need, and remember the gesture.
sites.after: The chest is empty. Someone on another road may need the same kindness.

sites.name: The Reed Bells
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: The tide speaks before the leaf. The leaf refuses to follow the ember. Let the remaining voice close the song.
sites.after: The bells have found their own voices. Eight memory threads are yours to carry.

sites.name: The Drowned Chime
sites.speaker: The Drowned Chime
sites.text: The Drowned Chime is held under by ropes tied to both banks. It remembers every crossing as a debt.|Break no bank. Choose where to stand, yield to the current, and make a space where both memories can meet.
sites.after: The old river stops passing through walls. It remains as a pale line on the water, visible at sunset.|Ivo hangs both maps beside the landing. One tells you how to travel. The other tells you why the village keeps a light on for strangers.

sites.name: The Ridge Path
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: The restored bell has opened the next road. You may travel onward or use the atlas to revisit any sanctuary you have reached.
sites.after: The road remains open. The spirits here will remember you.

sites.name: Floodwater Relay
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: A five-spirit endurance relay for a well-rested party. Conditions carry across rounds. There is no entry fee, and no penalty beyond returning to the sanctuary.|This optional trial rewards mastery and memory threads. The main road never requires repeating it.
sites.after: The relay is complete. You can return with another party whenever you wish.

sites.name: The Unused Ticket
sites.speaker: Ferryman Ivo
sites.text: A ferry ticket, never used: Passage for one person, three companions, and anything too important to name. The fare was paid by someone who did not leave their address.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

regions.request: Befriend a spirit from the Fen and read the memory at the old river marker. The ferryman needs a witness from each bank.

regions.name: Copperwind Rise
regions.subtitle: THE STORM IN THE WEATHER HOUSE
regions.arrival: The wind at Copperwind Rise blows toward a house with no doors. Every ribbon in the hills points to it. Every weather vane has bent trying to disagree.|Min, the weatherwright, has been sleeping under a table. She says this is the first honest forecast she has made all year.
regions.epilogue: Wind crosses the ridge in both directions. Min publishes a forecast with a blank space labeled perhaps.|Sable does not approve of the blank space. They help nail down the loose roof tiles anyway. Somewhere below, a seed reaches new ground.

sites.name: The Weather Inn
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: A warm light marks a place where nobody has to earn their rest. All your companions recover here. Three field remedies are replenished freely.|You can arrange your party, choose a lead, and tune a companion's temperament in the spirit book. Bond ranks unlock additional starting charms. No companion is lost when a challenge goes badly.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

sites.name: Min's Forecast
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: We used to predict the weather. Then people asked us to guarantee it. So we borrowed a note from the Crown and taught the wind to obey.|Now it follows the last instruction forever. In the garden, a cast can change the whole field. Wind is a direction and a duration, not just a pretty trail.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Crestwind Perch
sites.speaker: Galecrest / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Galecrest balances a feather against the entire western wind. When the feather falls, it laughs and tries again. It is not trying to stop the weather, only to meet it honestly.|FIELD NOTE / Its wind casts can change a whole exchange. Choose direction and strength deliberately; a helpful gust for one move may betray the next.
sites.after: The feather lands in your open hand.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: An Uncertain Direction
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: A keeper has prepared a two-spirit relay. Your party shares its condition across the rounds. Observe a telegraph, make a deliberate move, and leave energy for the answer.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: The Storm Drawing
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: Inside a fallen vane is a child's drawing of a storm. The rain is blue, the lightning is pink, and everybody is smiling.|Min recognizes her own handwriting. She used to love the thing she has spent her life trying to prevent.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Glasswing Ledge
sites.speaker: Glasswing / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Glasswing is repairing a broken window with pieces of its own reflection. Each pane shows the garden a moment before you arrive. The last pane is deliberately left empty.|FIELD NOTE / A fragile ranged spirit needs clear sightlines. Close a lane with terrain or force it to turn before a shot.
sites.after: It gives you the empty pane. A reflection, it seems, should always have somewhere new to go.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: Crosswind Practice
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: The second relay asks you to read the whole garden: obstacles, the central sanctuary, and the direction of the wind. Winning by holding ground is as valid as a knockout.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Ribbon Meadow
sites.speaker: Ribbonape / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Ribbonape has tied the mill's sails into an enormous bow. The miller is furious until the bow catches a wind the old sails could never use. Neither will admit who had the better idea.|FIELD NOTE / Mobility creates angles, but each arrival still needs a follow-up. Guard the landing space instead of chasing the entire path.
sites.after: A loose ribbon loops around your wrist, with enough room to slip free.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Laundry Knot
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: A Ribbonape has tied every laundry line into one enormous knot. The villagers call it sabotage. The youngest washer calls it a climbing frame.|You help move the knot to an empty meadow. The Ribbonape follows, delighted that someone finally understood the invitation.|REQUEST / Ring the local bell puzzle and befriend a spirit of the Rise. The mill needs a new song and someone who can carry it.
sites.after: Some problems become smaller when someone takes time to ask the right question.|Your companions gain 60 bond experience. You receive 12 memory threads and a keepsake recorded in the journal.

sites.name: A Door for the Wind
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: The third relay changes the opposing species. A strategy that chased the first spirit may exhaust itself against the next. Choose your lead before entering.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Nectar Orchard
sites.speaker: Nectarbat / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Nectarbat delivers pollen to the windmill's painted flowers. Nobody has told it they cannot bloom. The painted flowers are looking unusually bright this year.|FIELD NOTE / Airy movement is still a commitment. Use range and terrain to make its next pass predictable, rather than trying to mirror every turn.
sites.after: A dusting of pollen settles over your field book.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Shutter Debate
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: Sable calls the weather house a success. No roof has blown away in ten years. Min asks how many seeds have crossed the ridge.|Neither answer erases the other. You open the shutters one at a time. The first returning breeze smells of an orchard nobody here has visited.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: The Open Weather House
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: The last road trial asks you to bring everything together. Stop when an art requires planting. A short dodge creates an opening; endless sideways travel spends your recovery.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Flint Roost
sites.speaker: Flintroc / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Flintroc strikes sparks from the highest stone on the Rise. Each spark becomes a brief imitation of a star. On cloudy nights, the village climbs the hill to watch.|FIELD NOTE / A flying entry has to choose where it finishes. Threaten that destination, and use wind to change the approach rather than merely following it.
sites.after: It leaves one piece of flint in the circle of your companions.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: Roofmender's Chest
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: A traveller has left supplies for whoever follows: five memory threads and two field remedies. Nothing here has a price tag. Take what you need, and remember the gesture.
sites.after: The chest is empty. Someone on another road may need the same kindness.

sites.name: The Vane Bells
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: The ember calls from the high cliff. The leaf answers last. The tide carries the answer between them.
sites.after: The bells have found their own voices. Eight memory threads are yours to carry.

sites.name: The Brass Horizon
sites.speaker: The Brass Horizon
sites.text: The Brass Horizon turns like an enormous compass. Its needle points at whatever you fear most.|Commit to a route, then change it for a reason. A sideways circle will spend your breath without taking you anywhere.
sites.after: Wind crosses the ridge in both directions. Min publishes a forecast with a blank space labeled perhaps.|Sable does not approve of the blank space. They help nail down the loose roof tiles anyway. Somewhere below, a seed reaches new ground.

sites.name: The Orchard Road
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: The restored bell has opened the next road. You may travel onward or use the atlas to revisit any sanctuary you have reached.
sites.after: The road remains open. The spirits here will remember you.

sites.name: Stormfront Relay
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: A five-spirit endurance relay for a well-rested party. Conditions carry across rounds. There is no entry fee, and no penalty beyond returning to the sanctuary.|This optional trial rewards mastery and memory threads. The main road never requires repeating it.
sites.after: The relay is complete. You can return with another party whenever you wish.

sites.name: Instrument Plate
sites.speaker: Weatherwright Min
sites.text: Weather house instruction plate: If conditions differ from expectation, record the difference before correcting the instrument. Someone has scratched out correcting and written blaming.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

regions.request: Ring the local bell puzzle and befriend a spirit of the Rise. The mill needs a new song and someone who can carry it.

regions.name: Orchard of Names
regions.subtitle: THE FRUIT NOBODY CAN REMEMBER
regions.arrival: Every tree in the orchard grows a different memory. Weddings ripen in gold. Apologies taste like green pears. The oldest tree bears fruit so heavy that its branches touch the earth.|Elin offers you a basket and asks you not to eat anything until you know whose it is.
regions.epilogue: The trees begin ripening at different times. The harvest becomes inconvenient, then abundant.|Elin returns a basket of memories to their owners. Sable carries one fruit all afternoon before deciding to eat it. They do not tell you what it tastes like.

sites.name: The Grafting House
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: A warm light marks a place where nobody has to earn their rest. All your companions recover here. Three field remedies are replenished freely.|You can arrange your party, choose a lead, and tune a companion's temperament in the spirit book. Bond ranks unlock additional starting charms. No companion is lost when a challenge goes badly.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

sites.name: Elin's Basket
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: The Census stored names here before there were enough books. A tree can hold a family for centuries. But the Crown has started harvesting fruit before it ripens.|A sanctuary is strongest when someone chooses to stay. Learn to hold a place without chasing every threat beyond its edge.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Sunlit Grove
sites.speaker: Sunstag / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Sunstag stands where the orchard receives its first light. Its antlers hold a dawn that the clouds have not reached. The fruit beneath it ripens one careful day at a time.|FIELD NOTE / Long approaches announce a commitment. Hold a useful angle and leave room to step aside when the charge begins.
sites.after: It lowers its antlers just enough to share the morning.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: Holding the Clearing
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: A keeper has prepared a two-spirit relay. Your party shares its condition across the rounds. Observe a telegraph, make a deliberate move, and leave energy for the answer.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: The Erased Name
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: You find a memory of Nara laughing with a spirit whose name has been erased. On the reverse of the leaf: It was never mine. I wish I had understood that sooner.|The missing name has left a hole in the page. A Mosswarden carries the page carefully, as if the hole might break.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Mantis Walk
sites.speaker: Thornmantis / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Thornmantis is cutting ribbons for the orchard festival. Every cut is exact. When a child asks for a crooked ribbon, it has to sit down and think for a very long time.|FIELD NOTE / Its precise strike becomes dangerous after you commit. Bait the preparation and change range before the cut lands.
sites.after: The crooked ribbon is its proudest work.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Patient Garden
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: The second relay asks you to read the whole garden: obstacles, the central sanctuary, and the direction of the wind. Winning by holding ground is as valid as a knockout.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Moss Court
sites.speaker: Mosswarden / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Mosswarden tends a circle of seedlings planted by people who never returned. It knows every seedling by name. It asks you to remember one, so it can finally take a day away.|FIELD NOTE / A patient keeper builds strength around a position. Contest the garden early, or make it spend that strength defending an empty lane.
sites.after: The smallest seedling receives a careful promise. The warden uncurls its roots.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: A Place for the Forgotten
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: A Gravemole keeps burying fallen fruit under unmarked stones. Elin wants the fruit back. The mole wants the forgotten to have somewhere quiet.|You mark a corner of the orchard as a garden of names that no longer need an owner. Nothing there is for sale.|REQUEST / Meet all five orchard spirits at least once. The names on these ribbons should belong to neighbours, not an inventory.
sites.after: Some problems become smaller when someone takes time to ask the right question.|Your companions gain 60 bond experience. You receive 12 memory threads and a keepsake recorded in the journal.

sites.name: Roots and Room
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: The third relay changes the opposing species. A strategy that chased the first spirit may exhaust itself against the next. Choose your lead before entering.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: The Burial Garden
sites.speaker: Gravemole / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Gravemole has been burying old nameplates in pairs. One belongs to a person; the other is blank. It says everyone should have room for a name they choose later.|FIELD NOTE / The ground can hide a route, but an emergence has a destination. Use the objective to make it come to a place you can defend.
sites.after: A blank clay tablet joins the things in your satchel.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The First Census
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: Sable knows the erased name. It belonged to the first spirit entered into the Census: Hush. The records say it volunteered to hold the valley's dangerous memories.|Records can be exact about everything except whether someone was free to refuse. Sable closes the book before answering.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: The Harvest We Share
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: The last road trial asks you to bring everything together. Stop when an art requires planting. A short dodge creates an opening; endless sideways travel spends your recovery.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Hookthorn Bower
sites.speaker: Hooklynx / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Hooklynx has caught the orchard moon in a branch and will not let go. It is a silver festival lantern. This distinction matters very little to the lynx.|FIELD NOTE / A catch is most dangerous when it starts a sequence. Keep a reserve for the answer and do not stand at the same comfortable distance forever.
sites.after: It releases the lantern after you promise to bring it back next season.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Seed Chest
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: A traveller has left supplies for whoever follows: five memory threads and two field remedies. Nothing here has a price tag. Take what you need, and remember the gesture.
sites.after: The chest is empty. Someone on another road may need the same kindness.

sites.name: The Orchard Bells
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: The leaf opens the gate. The ember will only enter after the tide. No voice is repeated.
sites.after: The bells have found their own voices. Eight memory threads are yours to carry.

sites.name: The Root Choir
sites.speaker: The Root Choir
sites.text: The Root Choir is a grove that learned to sing with one voice. Its roots have grown around one another so tightly that none can move.|Win a place in the center, then make room for another voice. The orchard needs harmony with gaps in it.
sites.after: The trees begin ripening at different times. The harvest becomes inconvenient, then abundant.|Elin returns a basket of memories to their owners. Sable carries one fruit all afternoon before deciding to eat it. They do not tell you what it tastes like.

sites.name: The Kiln Road
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: The restored bell has opened the next road. You may travel onward or use the atlas to revisit any sanctuary you have reached.
sites.after: The road remains open. The spirits here will remember you.

sites.name: Harvest Relay
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: A five-spirit endurance relay for a well-rested party. Conditions carry across rounds. There is no entry fee, and no penalty beyond returning to the sanctuary.|This optional trial rewards mastery and memory threads. The main road never requires repeating it.
sites.after: The relay is complete. You can return with another party whenever you wish.

sites.name: Three Hands
sites.speaker: Orchard Keeper Elin
sites.text: A grafting note in three hands: This branch came from a tree that no longer exists. It is not the same tree. It is not nothing. Please stop asking it to choose.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

regions.request: Meet all five orchard spirits at least once. The names on these ribbons should belong to neighbours, not an inventory.

regions.name: Emberkiln
regions.subtitle: THE FURNACE THAT CANNOT REST
regions.arrival: The kilns of Emberkiln have burned through three generations without going cold. The city is famous for bells that never crack. Its workers are famous for never taking a day off.|Rua shows you a perfect bell and the bandages on her hands. Only one of these appears in the city's advertisements.
regions.epilogue: For one night the furnace goes dark. The city hears rain on its roofs for the first time in living memory.|Rua starts the morning fire by hand. She hangs the crooked bell above the door and closes the workshop before sunset.

sites.name: The Cooling House
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: A warm light marks a place where nobody has to earn their rest. All your companions recover here. Three field remedies are replenished freely.|You can arrange your party, choose a lead, and tune a companion's temperament in the spirit book. Bond ranks unlock additional starting charms. No companion is lost when a challenge goes badly.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

sites.name: Rua's Furnace
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: A spirit can give more than it has for a while. So can a person. The Crown taught our furnace to treat every pause as a fault.|Fire spreads across oil. Water clears it. Energy spent in one moment is missing from the next. Start there. We have forgotten how to stop.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Copper Spark
sites.speaker: Voltjack / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: The old copper fence rings whenever Voltjack races past. It has been playing the same unfinished tune for days. You hear the missing note in the pause between two sparks.|FIELD NOTE / Fast entries spend energy quickly. A lateral dodge can answer the commitment; permanent retreat gives it the whole garden.
sites.after: For the first time, the fence is quiet between songs. Voltjack waits for you to begin the next one.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Cost of Chasing
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: A keeper has prepared a two-spirit relay. Your party shares its condition across the rounds. Observe a telegraph, make a deliberate move, and leave energy for the answer.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: The Crooked Bell
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: An Anvilnewt has made a tiny bell with a crooked rim. It rings two notes at once. Rua calls it defective, then asks to hear it again.|The second note reminds her of her father humming while he worked. His bells were never as perfect as hers.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Ash Spiral
sites.speaker: Ashram / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Ashram has rebuilt the kiln's cold fire from a memory of warmth. It guards the ember fiercely, although the potter keeps reminding it that fire grows by being shared.|FIELD NOTE / A powerful charge needs a line and a commitment. Obstacles and late lateral dodges change the value of that line.
sites.after: One ember becomes two without either growing smaller.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: Banking the Flame
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: The second relay asks you to read the whole garden: obstacles, the central sanctuary, and the direction of the wind. Winning by holding ground is as valid as a knockout.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Anvil Yard
sites.speaker: Anvilnewt / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Anvilnewt taps at a cracked cup with a hammer larger than itself. The repair is terrible. The cup's owner keeps using it because it has never held so much care.|FIELD NOTE / Short reach and heavy preparation create clear windows. Make it turn, but do not spend all your breath circling a strike you could simply leave.
sites.after: The new crack becomes a gold-colored seam.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: Lunch for Slagjaw
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: A Slagjaw is swallowing discarded metal and coughing up nails. The apprentices have begun leaving it lunch in a bucket marked recycling.|Rua asks you to find out whether it likes the work. The spirit tips over the bucket and takes a nap. That seems like a useful answer.|REQUEST / Complete the first two Emberkiln road trials and befriend a local spirit. The smith needs a partner who knows when to set the hammer down.
sites.after: Some problems become smaller when someone takes time to ask the right question.|Your companions gain 60 bond experience. You receive 12 memory threads and a keepsake recorded in the journal.

sites.name: A Cool Place
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: The third relay changes the opposing species. A strategy that chased the first spirit may exhaust itself against the next. Choose your lead before entering.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: The Smoke Walk
sites.speaker: Pyrelisk / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Pyrelisk has made its home in an abandoned oven. It keeps the bricks warm for a baker who moved away years ago. Today, somebody has left a fresh loaf at the door.|FIELD NOTE / Heat spreads through prepared surfaces. Think about the next patch that can ignite, not only the fire already visible.
sites.after: It follows the smell of the loaf instead of waiting for the old footsteps.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Heat Order
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: Sable arrives with an order to keep the furnace running. Turning it off will leave the mountain roads without heat.|You arrange warm shelters along the route before touching the furnace. Care is more work than giving an order, and more useful than simply refusing one.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Shelters Before Silence
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: The last road trial asks you to bring everything together. Stop when an art requires planting. A short dodge creates an opening; endless sideways travel spends your recovery.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: The Crucible
sites.speaker: Slagjaw / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Slagjaw chews the forge's broken tools into smooth dark stones. The smith uses them to build a garden wall. A tool does not have to work forever to remain useful.|FIELD NOTE / A durable close-range spirit wants a long, messy exchange. Make openings deliberate and avoid paying for damage that its next answer will undo.
sites.after: The wall gains a stone shaped a little like a smile.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: Apprentice Cache
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: A traveller has left supplies for whoever follows: five memory threads and two field remedies. Nothing here has a price tag. Take what you need, and remember the gesture.
sites.after: The chest is empty. Someone on another road may need the same kindness.

sites.name: The Kiln Bells
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: The tide cools the kiln after the ember. The leaf waits between the two.
sites.after: The bells have found their own voices. Eight memory threads are yours to carry.

sites.name: The Unbanked Heart
sites.speaker: The Unbanked Heart
sites.text: The Unbanked Heart glows through walls of slag. It attacks whenever its own heat rises, until the room has nowhere cool left.|Make a breathing window. Let a threat expire. The strongest move may be the one you can still afford after the flame passes.
sites.after: For one night the furnace goes dark. The city hears rain on its roofs for the first time in living memory.|Rua starts the morning fire by hand. She hangs the crooked bell above the door and closes the workshop before sunset.

sites.name: The Snow Road
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: The restored bell has opened the next road. You may travel onward or use the atlas to revisit any sanctuary you have reached.
sites.after: The road remains open. The spirits here will remember you.

sites.name: Crucible Relay
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: A five-spirit endurance relay for a well-rested party. Conditions carry across rounds. There is no entry fee, and no penalty beyond returning to the sanctuary.|This optional trial rewards mastery and memory threads. The main road never requires repeating it.
sites.after: The relay is complete. You can return with another party whenever you wish.

sites.name: The Old Workshop Rule
sites.speaker: Kilnmaster Rua
sites.text: Workshop rule, hidden under a newer sign: A tool may be replaced. A worker may rest. Neither is a failure of the craft.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

regions.request: Complete the first two Emberkiln road trials and befriend a local spirit. The smith needs a partner who knows when to set the hammer down.

regions.name: Winter Archive
regions.subtitle: A LIBRARY OF THINGS THAT ALMOST HAPPENED
regions.arrival: Snow falls upward outside the Winter Archive. Inside, books contain every decision the valley nearly made. The aisles are full of people looking for proof that another life would have been easier.|Sen is trying to close the library for the evening. It has been the same evening for seven years.
regions.epilogue: The snow falls down. Sen locks the library and goes home while there is still light in the sky.|One shelf remains open: unfinished books. Sable leaves a notebook there with their own name on the cover. Only the first page has been written.

sites.name: The Archive Hearth
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: A warm light marks a place where nobody has to earn their rest. All your companions recover here. Three field remedies are replenished freely.|You can arrange your party, choose a lead, and tune a companion's temperament in the spirit book. Bond ranks unlock additional starting charms. No companion is lost when a challenge goes badly.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

sites.name: Sen's Closing Time
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: The Crown asked us for the safest future. We gave it every future in which nothing changed. It has been trying to make one of them happen ever since.|Ice carries momentum. Braking takes room. A plan should leave space for the moment after you decide it was wrong.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Rime Garden
sites.speaker: Rimehare / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Rimehare keeps freezing the edge of a puddle, then breaking it with one soft paw. Each circle catches a different sky. It wants to know whether tomorrow will fit inside the same water.|FIELD NOTE / Ice preserves momentum. Begin braking before the telegraph closes, and save a dodge for a direction change that walking cannot make.
sites.after: It leaves a ring of frost around your footprint, then hops out of it.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: Room to Brake
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: A keeper has prepared a two-spirit relay. Your party shares its condition across the rounds. Observe a telegraph, make a deliberate move, and leave energy for the answer.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: The Blank Book
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: You find a book titled The Road Not Taken by Nara. Every page is blank except the last: I would still have been afraid.|Sen says most visitors hate that book. It refuses to tell them that a different choice would have made them a different person.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Mirror Landing
sites.speaker: Ironmoth / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: An iron moth circles the Archive's oldest hinge. It is polishing the rust with silver dust. The librarian complains about the noise, but leaves the door open every night.|FIELD NOTE / Armor buys time to hold a position. Make each exchange count instead of feeding it many low-value commitments.
sites.after: A stubborn hinge swings freely as you leave. The moth follows the sound.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: A Turn Before the Step
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: The second relay asks you to read the whole garden: obstacles, the central sanctuary, and the direction of the wind. Winning by holding ground is as valid as a knockout.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Clockwork Pool
sites.speaker: Clockfin / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Clockfin swims through the air above a clock that runs backward. The librarian has stopped correcting it. Once a week, it gives someone a minute they thought they had lost.|FIELD NOTE / Repeated patterns are a resource to a patient controller. Break your timing and avoid answering every cast with the same dodge.
sites.after: It spends one whole minute listening to you say nothing.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Overdue Ending
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: A Clockfin has been returning the same overdue book every morning. The librarian keeps lending it back because the ending changes.|You sit together and read the new ending. It is ordinary and happy. The Clockfin finally lets the book stay on the shelf.|REQUEST / Read four memory markers anywhere along the road. The missing page was scattered into the stories people kept telling.
sites.after: Some problems become smaller when someone takes time to ask the right question.|Your companions gain 60 bond experience. You receive 12 memory threads and a keepsake recorded in the journal.

sites.name: The Thin Ice
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: The third relay changes the opposing species. A strategy that chased the first spirit may exhaust itself against the next. Choose your lead before entering.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: The Bell Stacks
sites.speaker: Bellox / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Bellox carries a bell whose note can only be heard after it fades. The archivist has filled six books describing the silence afterward. Bellox would rather go for a walk.|FIELD NOTE / Broad control threatens the space around a heavy body. Approach with a purpose, then allow time to recover outside that space.
sites.after: The seventh book remains empty. The walk is worth more.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: Sable's Unfinished Book
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: Sable is reading a future in which the Crown succeeds. Nobody is hurt. Nobody leaves. Nobody learns a new name.|They close the book without finishing it. For the first time, they ask what you think should happen next, and wait for an answer.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: A Future with Weather
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: The last road trial asks you to bring everything together. Stop when an art requires planting. A short dodge creates an opening; endless sideways travel spends your recovery.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Copper Gallery
sites.speaker: Coppergecko / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Coppergecko lives inside the Archive's electrical lamps. It warms one lamp at a time, according to a schedule nobody understands. The oldest reader always gets the first light.|FIELD NOTE / Charged ground changes the value of a wet lane. Watch the surface reaction as closely as the original projectile.
sites.after: A small copper footprint appears on the reading desk.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Reading Chest
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: A traveller has left supplies for whoever follows: five memory threads and two field remedies. Nothing here has a price tag. Take what you need, and remember the gesture.
sites.after: The chest is empty. Someone on another road may need the same kindness.

sites.name: The Frozen Bells
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: The tide comes first, the leaf last. The Archive has misplaced the middle word.
sites.after: The bells have found their own voices. Eight memory threads are yours to carry.

sites.name: The Still Pendulum
sites.speaker: The Still Pendulum
sites.text: The Still Pendulum counts each possible mistake before allowing a second to pass. Its garden is a sheet of mirror ice.|Turn before accelerating. Plant before casting. You do not need the perfect future. You need enough footing to meet the one that arrives.
sites.after: The snow falls down. Sen locks the library and goes home while there is still light in the sky.|One shelf remains open: unfinished books. Sable leaves a notebook there with their own name on the cover. Only the first page has been written.

sites.name: The Coastal Stair
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: The restored bell has opened the next road. You may travel onward or use the atlas to revisit any sanctuary you have reached.
sites.after: The road remains open. The spirits here will remember you.

sites.name: Mirror Relay
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: A five-spirit endurance relay for a well-rested party. Conditions carry across rounds. There is no entry fee, and no penalty beyond returning to the sanctuary.|This optional trial rewards mastery and memory threads. The main road never requires repeating it.
sites.after: The relay is complete. You can return with another party whenever you wish.

sites.name: An Uncertainty
sites.speaker: Archivist Sen
sites.text: Archive classification, penciled beneath a gold plaque: An uncertainty is not an error. Please do not shelve it with the accidents.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

regions.request: Read four memory markers anywhere along the road. The missing page was scattered into the stories people kept telling.

regions.name: Inkshore
regions.subtitle: LETTERS TO SOMEONE WHO HAS NOT ARRIVED
regions.arrival: At Inkshore, the sea washes letters onto the beach. Some were sent yesterday. Some will not be written for another hundred years. Oru sorts them by the sound they make when opened.|The quietest letters are kept in a box without a lock. Nobody has asked to read one until now.
regions.epilogue: The letters stop arriving in piles. Oru opens the quiet box and begins delivering them one at a time.|At the horizon, a dark tower lights one small window. For the first time in years, something inside is expecting a visitor.

sites.name: The Post House
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: A warm light marks a place where nobody has to earn their rest. All your companions recover here. Three field remedies are replenished freely.|You can arrange your party, choose a lead, and tune a companion's temperament in the spirit book. Bond ranks unlock additional starting charms. No companion is lost when a challenge goes badly.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

sites.name: The Quiet Box
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: Hush wrote to Nara every year. At first the letters asked when the work would end. Later they asked whether the valley still had birds.|The Census filed them as maintenance reports. The last letter contains a drawing of a door. Help me find the others.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Crescent Beach
sites.speaker: Gloamcat / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Something has stolen all the shadows from the pier. Gloamcat has tucked them under its tail to keep them warm. It will return them when the lamps stop pretending it is still afternoon.|FIELD NOTE / Watch facing and commitment rather than the prettiest effect. A patient defense can catch its return from an entry.
sites.after: Your shadow comes back with a small, companionable curl at its edge.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: An Echo Left Behind
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: A keeper has prepared a two-spirit relay. Your party shares its condition across the rounds. Observe a telegraph, make a deliberate move, and leave energy for the answer.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: The First Letter
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: The oldest letter is not a plea. It is a cheerful account of the first day at the Crown. Hush was proud to help.|A promise can begin freely and become a cage when nobody remembers to ask again. You copy the whole letter, including the cheerful part.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Prism Shoal
sites.speaker: Prismray / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: A prism spirit hangs above a tide pool, sorting moonlight into colors nobody has named. It tries to hand you violet, but the color slips between your fingers.|FIELD NOTE / Reflections and projectiles reward careful aim. Terrain breaks clean lanes; chasing its body alone can miss the real threat.
sites.after: A little rainbow remains on the blank page even when you close the book.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Returning Wave
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: The second relay asks you to read the whole garden: obstacles, the central sanctuary, and the direction of the wind. Winning by holding ground is as valid as a knockout.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Candle Cove
sites.speaker: Waxwyrm / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Waxwyrm carries a candle through the sea wind. It shields the flame with its own soft body. There are a hundred burned-out wicks behind it, and it remembers each light fondly.|FIELD NOTE / Lingering zones reshape safe space over time. Decide where the next exchange will happen before the current one ends.
sites.after: The candle burns lower, then steadier.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Second Laugh
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: An Echofin repeats the last laugh it heard. Its owner died years ago. The neighbours want it silenced because the sound hurts.|You help them listen together. By evening, the spirit has learned a second laugh. It keeps the first one too.|REQUEST / Restore six sanctuary bells. The lighthouse cannot answer a valley that has forgotten how to call.
sites.after: Some problems become smaller when someone takes time to ask the right question.|Your companions gain 60 bond experience. You receive 12 memory threads and a keepsake recorded in the journal.

sites.name: Between Two Tides
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: The third relay changes the opposing species. A strategy that chased the first spirit may exhaust itself against the next. Choose your lead before entering.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: The Dune Walk
sites.speaker: Duneskink / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Duneskink carries sand from a beach that no longer exists. It pours a little into each new footprint so the old shore can keep traveling.|FIELD NOTE / Concealment and repositioning reward observation. The objective and existing terrain can tell you where an unseen route is likely to end.
sites.after: Your tracks shine pale against the dark sand.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: A Reply by Hand
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: Sable finds the instruction that stopped the letters being delivered. Their predecessor signed it. Every keeper after them renewed it without reading.|Sable writes a reply by hand: I am sorry. We are coming. They ask you to carry it because the official post still leads back to the Crown.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: The Letter We Carry
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: The last road trial asks you to bring everything together. Stop when an art requires planting. A short dodge creates an opening; endless sideways travel spends your recovery.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Echo Inlet
sites.speaker: Echofin / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Echofin lives in the pause after the lighthouse bell. It repeats the last thing a traveller says, but in the voice they had as a child. Most travellers stay for a second conversation.|FIELD NOTE / A repeated effect may arrive after the first danger passes. Leave your escape route open until the whole pattern has finished.
sites.after: Your echo answers with a laugh you had almost forgotten.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Postbag
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: A traveller has left supplies for whoever follows: five memory threads and two field remedies. Nothing here has a price tag. Take what you need, and remember the gesture.
sites.after: The chest is empty. Someone on another road may need the same kindness.

sites.name: The Tide Bells
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: The leaf rises before the ember. The tide will not be first or last. Listen to the space between.
sites.after: The bells have found their own voices. Eight memory threads are yours to carry.

sites.name: The Unsent Tide
sites.speaker: The Unsent Tide
sites.text: The Unsent Tide has learned every word except goodbye. It returns every wave to the same shore.|Find a clean angle through the echoes. Let something pass without following it. You cannot carry every letter at once.
sites.after: The letters stop arriving in piles. Oru opens the quiet box and begins delivering them one at a time.|At the horizon, a dark tower lights one small window. For the first time in years, something inside is expecting a visitor.

sites.name: The Crown Stair
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: The restored bell has opened the next road. You may travel onward or use the atlas to revisit any sanctuary you have reached.
sites.after: The road remains open. The spirits here will remember you.

sites.name: Echo Relay
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: A five-spirit endurance relay for a well-rested party. Conditions carry across rounds. There is no entry fee, and no penalty beyond returning to the sanctuary.|This optional trial rewards mastery and memory threads. The main road never requires repeating it.
sites.after: The relay is complete. You can return with another party whenever you wish.

sites.name: Whoever Comes After
sites.speaker: Postkeeper Oru
sites.text: An envelope addressed only to Whoever Comes After: You do not owe us the life we expected. We hope you find a life you can share.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

regions.request: Restore six sanctuary bells. The lighthouse cannot answer a valley that has forgotten how to call.

regions.name: The Hush Crown
regions.subtitle: A DOOR THAT OPENS FROM BOTH SIDES
regions.arrival: The Crown is smaller than it looked from the valley. There is no throne. There are shelves, kettles, unfinished letters, and eight ropes passing through the ceiling.|Hush has been living here for a very long time. It has kept a place at the table for Nara.
regions.epilogue: The ropes fall quiet. Hush leaves the room through an ordinary door. Outside, it asks the name of a bird.|Nara answers. Sable writes it down, then leaves the rest of the page blank. Your companions wait at the bend in the road. There are places you have not visited together.

sites.name: The Waiting Room
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: A warm light marks a place where nobody has to earn their rest. All your companions recover here. Three field remedies are replenished freely.|You can arrange your party, choose a lead, and tune a companion's temperament in the spirit book. Bond ranks unlock additional starting charms. No companion is lost when a challenge goes badly.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

sites.name: The Keys
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: I thought a good system was one nobody had to question. Then I met the people living in its exceptions.|Hush cannot simply leave. Every bell is tied through its name. We have restored the other seven; now we must show that they can hold the road together.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: Basalt Threshold
sites.speaker: Basaltusk / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: The last intact bridge rests on Basaltusk's back. It has held still so long that flowers have taken root in its stone. Before it can follow you, it needs to remember that moving is allowed.|FIELD NOTE / Respect its turning radius and committed strikes. It cannot answer both sides at once, but a careless close approach is costly.
sites.after: The bridge holds after it steps away. Sometimes a promise finishes without breaking.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: A Burden Shared
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: A keeper has prepared a two-spirit relay. Your party shares its condition across the rounds. Observe a telegraph, make a deliberate move, and leave energy for the answer.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Nara's Return
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: Nara arrives carrying the first field book. She remembers the erased name at last. Hush does not rush to forgive her.|They sit across the table while you prepare the garden. There are some conversations a hero cannot complete for someone else.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: The Hollow Garden
sites.speaker: Nullurchin / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Nullurchin rests in the silence between two bells. Every time someone tries to name the silence, it grows another little spike. You offer it a quiet place in the book instead.|FIELD NOTE / A denied cast can ruin a burst sequence. Keep energy for a second plan and separate your approach from your strongest commitment.
sites.after: The quiet place remains quiet. The spirit seems pleased.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: No One Carries All
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: The second relay asks you to read the whole garden: obstacles, the central sanctuary, and the direction of the wind. Winning by holding ground is as valid as a knockout.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Moonlit Rest
sites.speaker: Mooncalf / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Mooncalf drinks from a basin that reflects no stars. It has been keeping them safe inside its pale coat until the Crown remembers how to make a night worth shining into.|FIELD NOTE / A gentle-looking support can make a long exchange favorable. Pressure its recovery windows while preserving your own.
sites.after: One star returns to the water. The others will follow when they are ready.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: An Ordinary Blanket
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: A Mooncalf has been sleeping in the tower's shadow. It dreams the dreams Hush no longer has room to dream.|You leave a blanket beside it. Saving the valley has not made its nights warm. There is still ordinary work to do.|REQUEST / Befriend all forty species. This final page should make room for every way a spirit can choose to be.
sites.after: Some problems become smaller when someone takes time to ask the right question.|Your companions gain 60 bond experience. You receive 12 memory threads and a keepsake recorded in the journal.

sites.name: The Last Census
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: The third relay changes the opposing species. A strategy that chased the first spirit may exhaust itself against the next. Choose your lead before entering.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: Ink Gallery
sites.speaker: Inkheron / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Inkheron has written a sentence across the Crown's broken steps. Rain washes it away every evening. It writes the sentence again every morning, changing one word each time.|FIELD NOTE / Long, deliberate attacks punish a stable line. Shift early, then plant when the heron is busy recovering.
sites.after: Today, the sentence leaves room for your answer.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: A Way to Change
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: The Census offers you its keys. You could keep the Crown, distribute its burden, and make a gentler order. Or open it completely and let the valley negotiate a new road.|Sable will help with either choice. They ask only that you leave a way for the next keeper to change their mind.
sites.after: The conversation has changed what you know. The next marked place on the road is now open.

sites.name: The Open Question
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: The last road trial asks you to bring everything together. Stop when an art requires planting. A short dodge creates an opening; endless sideways travel spends your recovery.
sites.after: The road trial is complete. Your companions carry the experience together. A new chapter marker is waiting ahead.

sites.name: The Oath Gate
sites.speaker: Oathhound / FIELD ENCOUNTER
sites.text: Oathhound guards an open doorway. Nobody ordered it to stay; nobody has ever asked whether it would like to leave. You sit beside the door and tell it about the road.|FIELD NOTE / A protector is strongest when it can answer a clear threat. Feints and changes of pace matter as much as raw damage.
sites.after: The doorway remains open when the hound stands.|Trust grows through shared challenges. You may offer three memory threads after the first meeting, or return for another friendly encounter.

sites.name: The Guest Chest
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: A traveller has left supplies for whoever follows: five memory threads and two field remedies. Nothing here has a price tag. Take what you need, and remember the gesture.
sites.after: The chest is empty. Someone on another road may need the same kindness.

sites.name: The Eightfold Bells
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: The ember waits until both others have spoken. The tide speaks before the leaf. A crown belongs at the end.
sites.after: The bells have found their own voices. Eight memory threads are yours to carry.

sites.name: Hush, Keeper of Every Name
sites.speaker: Hush, Keeper of Every Name
sites.text: Hush steps into the garden wearing every promise it has ever made. It does not want to defeat you. It wants to know whether you will notice when it needs to stop.|This is a relay, not a sacrifice. Let your companions share the work. The road was never meant to be carried by one small spirit.
sites.after: The ropes fall quiet. Hush leaves the room through an ordinary door. Outside, it asks the name of a bird.|Nara answers. Sable writes it down, then leaves the rest of the page blank. Your companions wait at the bend in the road. There are places you have not visited together.

sites.name: The Unwritten Road
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: The restored bell has opened the next road. You may travel onward or use the atlas to revisit any sanctuary you have reached.
sites.after: The road remains open. The spirits here will remember you.

sites.name: The Long Relay
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: A five-spirit endurance relay for a well-rested party. Conditions carry across rounds. There is no entry fee, and no penalty beyond returning to the sanctuary.|This optional trial rewards mastery and memory threads. The main road never requires repeating it.
sites.after: The relay is complete. You can return with another party whenever you wish.

sites.name: The First Entry
sites.speaker: Sable
sites.text: The first entry in the Census: Name, Hush. Species, uncertain. Occupation, helping. Expected duration, until needed no longer. The renewal box was added later.
sites.after: This memory is now recorded in your field book.

regions.request: Befriend all forty species. This final page should make room for every way a spirit can choose to be.
